Module 12: Digital Scholarly Commentary — Learning Objectives

By the end of this module, students will be able to:

  • Classify scholarly commentary into distinct epistemological categories: philological/linguistic, historical/contextual, and intertextual text-reuse.
  • Encode granular inline and stand-off commentary notes in TEI P5 using <note>, <anchor>, and @target pointer mechanisms.
  • Apply algorithmic text-reuse discovery frameworks (such as Tesserae n-gram frequency matching) to detect intertextual allusions across classical and historical corpora.
  • Model annotations using the W3C Web Annotation Data Model, specifying targets, bodies, motivations, and selectors in JSON-LD.
  • Audit and vet AI-generated commentary notes, catching fabricated citations, anachronistic interpretations, and unsupported claims.
